summary: This note summarizes the Ottawa Senators' 2006-07 NHL season. After a poor start amid high personnel turnover and trade rumours about Daniel Alfredsson, the team climbed out of last place in its division, finished fourth in the Eastern Conference with 105 points, and then advanced through the playoffs to the Stanley Cup Finals by beating the Pittsburgh Penguins, New Jersey Devils and Buffalo Sabres.
one_line: Ottawa Senators' 2006-07 season, which ended with a Stanley Cup Finals run after playoff wins over Pittsburgh, New Jersey and Buffalo.
key_facts: The Ottawa Senators reached the Stanley Cup Finals in the 2006-07 season after qualifying for the playoffs in nine consecutive seasons.
The Senators had a high turnover of personnel and the disappointment of 2006 to overcome before the 2006-07 season.
The Senators started the 2006-07 season poorly.
Trade rumours swirled around Daniel Alfredsson for most of the last months of 2006.
The Ottawa Senators lifted themselves out of last place in their division to nearly catch the Buffalo Sabres by season's end.
The Ottawa Senators placed fourth in the Eastern Conference in 2006-07.
The Ottawa Senators finished the 2006-07 season with 105 points, their fourth straight 100-point season and sixth in the last eight.
In the playoffs, the 'CASH' line, goaltender Ray Emery, and the defence of Chris Phillips and Anton Volchenkov led the Ottawa Senators.
The Ottawa Senators defeated the Pittsburgh Penguins in the playoffs.
The Ottawa Senators defeated the second-ranked New Jersey Devils in the playoffs.
The Ottawa Senators defeated the top-ranked Buffalo Sabres to advance to the Stanley Cup Finals.
